html:
The Minang are a Noongar people of the south coast of Western Australia, around King George Sound and the town of Albany. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were other Noongar groups: the Goreng to the east, the Kaniyang to the north and the Bibbulman to the west. The British navigator George Vancouver named King George Sound in 1791, and French and British ships called in after him.

In 1826 the British set up a small army post at King George Sound, the first European settlement in Western Australia, to keep the French out. Relations were at first fairly peaceful. A Minang man, Mokare, guided the settlers and became a friend of the post's surgeon. As farms spread after Western Australia became a colony, the Minang lost most of their land.
